title: Unified Knowledge-Action Ontology Architecture v1
goal: Determine whether a provenance-preserving typed ontology/knowledge-graph substrate can unify research knowledge representation with executor decision/action semantics—so accumulated knowledge can help determine what should be done next—without conflating scientific evidence with policy authority, and produce a bounded architecture/benchmark plan before any production mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The task recovers the actual current research-engine persistence architecture and schema from repository/runtime evidence, including authoritative evidence storage, normalized knowledge, relations, checkpoints, embeddings/search projections, and any graph-like structures already present.

The task recovers the actual workspace-control execution/policy representation, including task capsules, workflows, procedures, policy/authority boundaries, executor routing, state transitions, and receipts/evidence used to determine safe next actions.

The research clearly distinguishes epistemic knowledge (what is believed/observed/inferred) from normative/action knowledge (what is permitted/required/preferred) and from execution state (what has actually happened).

The MILCOM 2026 lead is investigated with public evidence: best-poster winner, Boeing employee in California, PhD student, author of a book beginning with 'The 4th Industrial Revolution:', and an autonomous-vehicle edge/cloud project using ontology/semantic graphs rather than raw sensor payloads. Identity and paper title are not claimed unless evidence converges.

A current external survey covers ontology engineering, semantic/knowledge graphs, RDF/OWL/property graphs, scene/semantic graphs, policy/rule engines, behavior trees/state machines/planning, neuro-symbolic systems, continual knowledge graphs, and knowledge-driven autonomous-agent architectures relevant to the hypothesis.

At least three materially distinct architecture families are compared, including a separated-but-linked research knowledge graph plus policy/action graph, a unified typed graph with strict layer/authority boundaries, and an event-sourced knowledge/action substrate with rebuildable graph projections.
The design preserves provenance, contradiction, temporal validity, confidence, source authority, supersession, and uncertainty rather than collapsing knowledge into one asserted world state.

No research fact, inferred relation, or model-generated edge can silently become executor authority; transitions from knowledge to action require explicit policy/authority semantics and auditable decision evidence.
Continual-learning semantics are defined as controlled append/update/versioning of evidence, derived knowledge, ontology mappings, and policy revisions rather than unconstrained self-modification.

The task evaluates whether the existing PostgreSQL + content-addressed artifact store + rebuildable pgvector/text/graph-projection strategy can host the proposed semantics before considering a new database technology.

A bounded prototype/benchmark contract is defined before implementation, measuring decision correctness, provenance traceability, contradiction handling, update behavior, retrieval/query utility, policy applicability, explainability, and failure isolation.

The final recommendation states whether to pursue, narrow, or reject the unified knowledge-action ontology hypothesis and provides a migration path that keeps current research-engine and workspace-control behavior rollback-safe.
constraints: This is a separate research/architecture task. Do not change the Local EXTRACT Wave 7 task, its scientific gates, or its next action because of ontology research.
Do not replace PostgreSQL, pgvector, the content-addressed artifact store, task capsules, workflows, or policy files merely because graph technology appears attractive.
Preserve authoritative source evidence as scientific truth; ontology/graph structures are derived semantic representations unless an existing project contract explicitly makes them authoritative.
Keep epistemic, normative/policy, and execution-state semantics explicitly typed and distinguishable even if represented in one physical graph.
Do not let unverified research claims, model-generated edges, or inferred correlations directly authorize executor actions.
Do not introduce autonomous policy self-modification. Policy/authority changes remain explicit, reviewable, versioned, and human-gated where currently required.
Do not silently reconcile contradictory evidence; preserve disagreement, context, temporal validity, and source provenance.
Do not infer the MILCOM researcher's identity from weak clues. Use public sources and label candidate matches/uncertainty until evidence converges.
Prefer architectural evidence and working implementations over ontology buzzwords or vendor claims.
No production mutation in workspace-control or research-engine is authorized during the initial research stages beyond this task capsule and derived handoff.
Any later prototype must be additive/rebuildable and must preserve current systems as the known-good rollback state.

notes:
Core hypothesis from the user: a durable data structure may be able to represent both accumulated knowledge about the world/research domain and the semantics that tell executors what action is appropriate in a given situation. The task must investigate this seriously while preventing a dangerous collapse of 'is true/believed' into 'is authorized/should execute'. The envisioned long-term system may support continual learning, research-gap discovery, and context-sensitive executor coordination, but those capabilities are hypotheses to evaluate rather than assumed goals.
